e.etymology: A modern American name that shares its sound with Amari, Avery and Ava.
From the English term of endearment, Old English deorling, dear little one. It is also an English and Scottish surname, as in the Darling family of Peter Pan.
e.note: Because darling is an everyday endearment, the name can be heard as a pet name instead of a given name.

e.meaning: faithful, wholehearted; from the Hebrew word for dog
e.etymology: A respelling of Caleb, from Hebrew Kalev, related to the word for dog and long read as a sign of loyalty. In the Bible Caleb is one of the two faithful spies sent into Canaan.
An elaborated spelling in the Kayleigh family: Kaleigh with a final -a, giving a sound close to Kaleah.
From the English bird name, Old English hafoc, and from the surname Hawk, once given to a falconer or to someone thought hawk-like.
An Arabic name usually derived from the root for height, giving the sense of exalted. Sumayyah bint Khayyat is revered as the first martyr of Islam.
A respelling of Silas with the Cy- of Cyrus. Silas is the New Testament short form of Silvanus, from Latin silva, forest.
From Yiddish hirsh, deer, the everyday counterpart of the Hebrew name Tzvi. In the US it is used mostly in Orthodox and Hasidic Jewish families.
From Arabic sabir, the one who is patient, from sabara, to endure. Patience, sabr, is a central virtue in Islam.
The Greek form of Luke and the source of Latin Lucas: Loukas, a man from Lucania in southern Italy. It is the name of the author of the third Gospel.
A spelling of Arabic Mu'adh, from the root for seeking refuge: one who is sheltered or protected. Mu'adh ibn Jabal was a noted companion of the Prophet Muhammad.
Best known from Erza Scarlet, a heroine of the manga and anime Fairy Tail. Erza is also a girl's name in Albania and Kosovo, and some uses are a rearranged Ezra.
e.note: Easily misread or autocorrected as Ezra.

assoc.t: Erza Scarlet, the armored mage of the anime Fairy Tail

e.etymology: A respelling of Zara with the X of Xena and Xavier. Zara entered English through 18th-century plays and is usually traced to Arabic Zahra, radiant or blossom.
A modern spelling close to Azaria and Azariah, a biblical Hebrew name meaning Yahweh has helped, from the root azar, to help.
The surname of Garrick Ollivander, the wandmaker in J.K. Rowling's Harry Potter books. As a first name it works as a longer form of Oliver with the nickname Ollie.

assoc.t: Ollivander, the wandmaker in Harry Potter

e.etymology: A spelling of Khalila, the feminine of Arabic Khalil, close friend.
A spelling of Elowen, from the Cornish word elowen, elm tree. It has been used as a given name only since the late 20th century.
A Spanish-language name, also spelled Yajaira, common in Caribbean and Mexican American families since the 1980s. Its origin is uncertain.
A surname, a variant of Spanish Montes, from monte, mountain or hill. As a first name it is mostly African American, in use since the 1970s.
A modern name that sits between Jocelyn and Jaclyn, also read as Jace plus the -lyn ending.
An English surname meaning son of Robin, the medieval pet form of Robert, bright fame. As a first name it is also popular in Latin America.
namesakes: Robinson Crusoe (castaway hero of Daniel Defoe's novel)

assoc.t: Jackie Robinson, who broke baseball's color barrier

e.etymology: From Arabic nasim, a soft, fresh breeze. The word passed into Persian and Urdu, where the name is given to both boys and girls.
An American respelling of Giovanna, the Italian feminine of Giovanni (John), from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious. The Gia- opening echoes Gia and Gianna.
A spelling of Montserrat, the saw-toothed mountain near Barcelona whose monastery holds a famous statue of the Virgin Mary. The name honors Our Lady of Montserrat.
The phonetic English spelling of Irish Eithne, an old name from a word for kernel or grain, borne by several early Irish saints and legendary queens.

assoc.t: Enya, Irish singer of Orinoco Flow and Only Time

e.etymology: A respelling of Colby, an English place name and surname from Old Norse: the farm of a man called Koli, a byname meaning dark or coal-black.

e.meaning: lord, ruler; a name of Shiva
e.etymology: A spelling of Ishaan, from Sanskrit Ishana, lord or ruler, a name of Shiva as guardian of the northeast.
The Hebrew form of Isaiah, short for Yeshayahu, Yahweh is salvation, the name of the great prophet. In the US it is used mostly in Orthodox Jewish families.
A spelling of Jaslyn or Jazlyn, modern American blends of Jasmine and the -lyn ending.
An English spelling of German Emmerich, a merger of old Germanic names ending in ric, ruler, among them Amalric, work-ruler. Saint Emeric was an 11th-century Hungarian prince.

e.meaning: ewe, as a form of Rachel; also Arabic for traveler
e.etymology: For girls, the Arabic and Persian form of Rachel, from Hebrew rahel, ewe. For boys it is a separate Arabic name meaning one who travels or sets out.
